mission_04: In-memory computing performs computation directly within memory devices, eliminating the von Neumann bottleneck of data movement between CPU and memory. Memristor crossbar arrays implement matrix-vector multiplication in a single analog step: input voltages are applied to rows, currents flow through memristors according to Ohm's law (I = V * G), and output currents are summed at columns via Kirchhoff's law. This achieves O(1) time complexity for matrix-vector multiplication regardless of matrix size. Differential pairs of crossbars handle signed weights (positive and negative conductances). In this mission, you implement a memristor crossbar that maps weights to conductance values, computes matrix-vector products using analog principles, handles signed weights with differential crossbar pairs, simulates device noise, and compares in-memory computation accuracy against ideal digital computation.
